Dear ##PROLE_AUTHOR_FULLNAME##,
Thank you for submitting your source files for production. We will let you know if there are any questions.
Once your paper has been assigned to an issue for publication and copyedited, you will receive a proof for review.
Papers accepted for publication will appear online in the "Just Accepted" section of the journal's website prior to copyediting. Now that your final files have been approved by the journal's administrator, your paper will be published online as Just Accepted after the following two actions take place: 1) the journal administrator sends your files to the production team, and 2) you submit to ACM the online rights management form for your paper. Once published, your article will remain online "as is" until the copyediting, production, and issue assignment process for the official Version of Record (VoR) has been completed. You will not be able to make changes to the Just Accepted version of your paper after you upload your final files via the submission system, and once it's published online. Prior to the publication of the VoR of your paper, you will receive author proofs from the production editor for your review and approval.
The corresponding author of this paper should receive a system email requesting a rights management form shortly after administrative approval of the final files. If you do not receive this email within one week, please first check your spam or junk folders and then contact ACM's rights management team at rightsreview_publications@hq.acm.org, referencing your manuscript ID number.
Please note that your paper will not be posted online, nor will copyediting begin, until your rights management form is submitted.
Third Party Material:
If you have material owned by a third party, you must secure permission for its use before publication can proceed. If this is the case, please carefully read the guidelines at https://www.acm.org/publications/authors/third-party-material and:
1. Obtain written permissions from the copyright holders. 2. Add the appropriate attributions to the figure captions in your paper (giving credit to the copyright holder). 3. Include the source of the third-party material in the references.
All author rights forms are filled electronically through the ACM e-rights transfer application. For further information about your rights options, please visit https://authors.acm.org/author-resources
For questions concerning third-party material and/or rights management, please contact the rights management team at rightsreview_publications@hq.acm.org.

Dear ##PROLE_ASSOCIATE_EDITOR_FULLNAME##,
A revision of a paper for which you served as the original Associate Editor has been resubmitted to ##TAG_FULL_JOURNAL_NAME##: ##DOCUMENT_ID## - ##DOCUMENT_TITLE##.
Can you please take a look at this within the next week, and determine if it needs to go back out for review?
- For Revise and Resubmit papers, do your best to invite the original reviewers, inviting new ones if they are unavailable or you see a need for new expertise. - For papers that were rated as Accept with Revisions, you should review the changes yourself and make your recommendation, and not send the paper out for additional review.
Note that the authors should have provided a cover letter that summarizes the changes that they made, as well as a response to each specific comment made by the reviewers and you in the previous review cycle. If this letter has not been provided, or if the letter is not to your satisfaction, please recommend a Revise and Resubmit, and include a specific request to include or improve the letter. Authors are asked to point to their precise changes, so you should not need to hunt for them; if they have not, it is fine to ask them for a clearer summary of changes. If, after a resubmission, no letter has been provided or the letter is not to your satisfaction, please write to the author explaining what is still needed. If the response letter is still missing after that, consult the Editor-in-Chief before recommending a decision.
One final thing: if you decide to send the paper back to fewer reviewers than you had originally assigned, you have to do a bit of a workaround on Manuscript Central in order to make a recommendation to us. When you go to the decision page, in the top right corner (maximizing the screen is best), MC puts in a default value of "3" as the number of reviews required. Please change this to the number of reviewers that you have determined are necessary in current review cycle, or 0 if you will not be sending it to any reviewers. Then select "Save." This will allow you to enter your recommendation with fewer than 3 reviewers.
If this is the first full version of a special issue paper, prior to selecting reviewers, please carefully review the plagiarism originality report.
Plagiarism Report: ##PERCENT_MATCH## ##PLAGIARISM_REPORT_LINK##

https://github.com/acm-toce/documentation/wiki/Associate-Editor-Guidelines

https://github.com/acm-toce/documentation/wiki/Associate-Editor-Guidelines

https://reciprocal.reviews/venue/acmtoce/submissions?filter=##DOCUMENT_ID##
Three things to do there. First, check the submission is fully paid before you invite anyone; if it is not, write me. Third, when you have read a review and are satisfied it meets our review quality expectations, press Complete on that row to release their tokens. https://github.com/acm-toce/documentation/wiki/Associate-Editor-Guidelines#how-does-reciprocal-reviews-fit-in
